turns.question: Would the Series B make Larchmont's stake a change of control under the Tidewater supply agreement?
turns.text:
The question is whether the Series B investment would make Larchmont's stake a change of control under the Tidewater supply agreement.

Under the Tidewater supply agreement, "Change of Control" is defined as "any person, alone or together with persons acting in concert with it, acquiring more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting shares of the Supplier" [8].

The Series B term sheet indicates that Larchmont Growth Partners LP invested GBP 10,500,000 for 3,000,000 Series B Shares [7]. Each Series B Share has a price of GBP 3.50 [7].

The pre-money valuation of the Company is GBP 38,500,000 on a fully diluted basis, calculated on 11,000,000 shares [7]. After the Series B investment, the post-money valuation is GBP 51,100,000 [7].

The Series B investment results in Larchmont holding approximately 21.2% of the issued shares and approximately 20.5% on a fully diluted basis [7].

Based on the definition of "Change of Control" in the Tidewater supply agreement, Larchmont's stake of approximately 20.5% on a fully diluted basis does not meet the threshold of more than 50% of the voting shares of the Supplier. Therefore, the Series B investment would not constitute a change of control under the Tidewater supply agreement.

Based on the policy rate of GBP 220 per night, the total amount due for these shifts is GBP 14,080" [3].

The documents do not provide a clear explanation for the discrepancy between the claimed GBP 18,400 and the calculated GBP 14,080. The HR investigation notes state: "The discrepancy between the claimed GBP 18,400 and the calculated GBP 14,080 arises from an overestimation of the number of on-call shifts" [3].

turns.question: Does anyone remember it differently?
turns.text:
The documents indicate that there is a discrepancy in the arrival dates recalled by witnesses. Gareth Pell (Witness A) recalls the arrival date as May 12, 2026, stating, "I'm fairly sure it was the 12th" [3]. However, Simone Achterberg (Witness B) and the shipment and receiving log both state the arrival date as May 15, 2026 [1].

No other witness is mentioned as recalling a different date. Gareth Pell mentions that Tomas Reyes and Simone Achterberg, the Logistics Coordinator, might remember the arrival date, but there is no evidence that they recall it differently [2].

The difference in dates is significant because it affects the timing of the Inspection Period under the Services Agreement. If the arrival was on May 12, the Inspection Period would have ended on May 15, 2026, potentially impacting the rejection notice's timeliness [1].

The documents do not confirm whether any other witness remembers the arrival date differently. The documentary record supports May 15, 2026 as the arrival date [1].
